title: Head injuries and falls
description: Injury to the head after a fall, blow, or accident. May involve concussion, skull fracture, or brain injury.

recognition_questions.q: Did the person lose consciousness, even briefly?
Are they confused, drowsy, or vomiting?
Is there a severe headache, or clear fluid from the ear or nose?

observable_symptoms: Bruising around eyes or behind ear
immediate_safety_warnings: Do not move the person if you suspect a neck/spine injury unless they are in danger.
If the person is unconscious but breathing, keep their airway open and do not move them.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Call 112 if the person lost consciousness, is confused, vomiting, or drowsy, or if it was a high-impact fall.
ordered_instructions.rationale: These are signs of serious brain injury.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Keep the person still. If conscious, ask them to lie down and keep their head and shoulders slightly raised.
Apply a cold compress (wrapped in cloth) to a visible bump for up to 20 minutes.
Check responsiveness and breathing every few minutes until help arrives.
ordered_instructions.rationale: A head injury can deteriorate quickly.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If the person is unconscious but breathing, place them in the recovery position and keep the airway open, supporting the neck.

actions_to_avoid: Do not move someone with a possible spine injury unless in danger.
Do not let the person drive or operate machinery after a head injury.
Do not give food or drink.
Do not press on a wound if you suspect a skull fracture.
Do not let a concussed person 'sleep it off' unobserved.

escalation_conditions.condition: Unequal pupils, clear fluid from ear/nose, bruising around eyes

escalation_conditions.action: Call 112; protect from injury; do not restrain

escalation_conditions.condition: Person becomes unconscious and stops breathing

equipment_requirements.item: Cold compress or ice pack wrapped in cloth

approved_alternatives.alternative: A cloth soaked in cold water, or frozen vegetables wrapped in a cloth

follow_up_requirements: Anyone with a head injury must be observed for 24 hours for worsening symptoms.
Seek urgent care if a severe headache, vomiting, confusion, drowsiness, or weakness develops later.

age_specific_pathways.infant: Any fall from a height or onto a hard surface in an infant needs urgent medical assessment even if they seem fine.
age_specific_pathways.child: Children with any head injury and vomiting, drowsiness, or confusion need urgent assessment.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
